title: A six-metabolite machine-learning panel and isovalerylcarnitine findings for gastric cancer
summary: In two multicenter cohorts totaling 597 people, LASSO feature selection and five machine-learning classifiers produced a six-metabolite plasma panel for gastric-cancer diagnosis, with AUCs of 0.947–0.982 in discovery and 0.920–0.951 in validation. The panel included isovalerylcarnitine (C5), which was lower in cancer plasma and paired tumor tissue; the paper further reported a Mendelian-randomization association and cell-assay evidence linking C5 treatment to reduced gastric-cancer cell migration and invasion through calpain-associated changes in VE-cadherin and MMP2.
ai_technology: LASSO regression score feature selection with neural-network, support-vector-machine, ridge-regression, logistic-regression and naive-Bayes classifiers
organization: Zhejiang Cancer Hospital and six collaborating clinical centers; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Zhejiang Chinese Medical University; Wenzhou Medical University; National Cancer Center/National Clinical Research Center for Cancer, China

evidence.tested: In two multicenter cohorts totaling 597 people, LASSO feature selection and five machine-learning classifiers produced a six-metabolite plasma panel for gastric-cancer diagnosis, with AUCs of 0.947–0.982 in discovery and 0.920–0.951 in validation.
evidence.unknown: The cohorts were case-control clinical samples and do not establish population-screening performance or improved patient outcomes. The validation cohort contained 453 participants from seven centers; no prospective care-impact trial was reported. Mendelian-randomization evidence is observational genetic-instrument analysis, and cell migration/invasion experiments do not establish a treatment effect in animals or people. The 2024 IDDF abstract (DOI 10.1136/gutjnl-2024-IDDF.267) is an earlier disclosure of this same project, not a separate discovery. Source checked; independent replication not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning feature selection narrowed replicated plasma metabolite signals to a six-feature diagnostic panel, and the specified classifiers constructed/evaluated diagnostic models. The C5 mechanistic work was follow-up metabolomics, Mendelian-randomization, proteomic-correlation and in-vitro experimentation; the record does not imply that machine learning alone established the mechanism.
